chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim al-Aḥmar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him: “May wudu (ablution) be performed from the leftover water of the wudu (ablution) of a menstruating woman?” He said: “No.”

So the proper way regarding these reports is what was detailed in the earlier reports, namely that if the woman is not trusted, then performing wudu (ablution) with her leftover water is not permissible. And it is possible that what is intended by them is a kind of recommendation, and what indicates that is what...

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation rather than obligation or prohibition
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports or hadiths under discussion
key_terms.فَضْلِ وُضُوءِ: the leftover water remaining from wudu (ablution)
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةً: considered trustworthy or reliable regarding purity

ai.seo_question: Can one perform wudu (ablution) using the leftover water from a menstruating woman’s wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on using the leftover water associated with the wudu (ablution) of a menstruating woman. It presents the apparent prohibition, then explains that the reports are to be understood in light of earlier narrations: where she is not trusted, it is not permissible, and the wording may also indicate a matter of recommendation.
